# DeskTop: Hanggang Umaga

> Windows desktop game where a top-down webcam turns real desk objects into 16-bit pixel art units. One to four players at one table move the objects by hand and give Taglish or English voice orders to survive Filipino folklore creatures for 8 turns until sunrise. Electron, React and TypeScript renderer, FastAPI, OpenCV and SQLite backend on 127.0.0.1, four Meta models (Muse Spark 1.3, SAM 3.1, Muse Image 1.0, Muse Voice Transcribe 1.0). A deterministic rules engine owns every number. Solo build by EHIBE for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026, Indie track.

Start with CLAUDE.md for current state, constraints and commands, then docs/README.md for the doc map. Each fact has one canonical file, named in its `canonical_for` front matter. Code beats docs.

- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): current state, pending queue, constraints, bugs, commands, agents and skills
- [Docs index](docs/README.md): every doc, read order by task, doc conventions

- [How to run](docs/how-to-run.md): player guide for the zip and from source

- [Powers](docs/game/powers.md): P01 to P12
- [Enemies](docs/game/enemies.md): aswang, tikbalang, kapre, manananggal, duwende
- [Waves and difficulty](docs/game/waves-and-difficulty.md): spawn table by turn
- [Combat math](docs/game/combat-math.md): damage, shields, walls, ties
- [Campaign progression](docs/game/campaign-progression.md): barrio level, badges, scars, returning objects
